_comment: Configuration for the Farm Water Analysis dashboard generator (lib/build_dashboard.py). Edit these values as the garden / irrigation plan changes; no code changes needed.

probes._setpoint_removed: REMOVED 2026-08-22. `setpoint` (tomato 62, pepper 35) is gone from config, analyze.py and the dashboard. It was an EcoWitt app ALERT THRESHOLD hand-set by Justin, never derived from this dataset, and un-derivable in absolute terms while both probes run FACTORY calibration (0%AD = air, 100%AD = submerged), where '%' is an index on that calibration rather than volumetric water content. Scoring irrigation against it was measuring the operator's guess, not the soil. It is replaced by the `bands` block on each probe below, which IS derived from this dataset. Do not reintroduce a single-number setpoint; the two thresholds that matter are a ceiling and a floor, and they mean different things.
probes._bands_provenance: DERIVED 2026-08-22 from 15,569 readings (2026-06-29 → 2026-08-22) against Open-Meteo hourly ET0, by lib/derive_bands.py. METHOD, and the reason this needs no soil calibration: partition moisture loss by whether the atmosphere was demanding water at the time. NIGHT (ET0 = 0) — any moisture leaving the soil in the dark is not being transpired, so it is drainage. Binning night loss rate by moisture level gives a flat near-zero floor that jumps by an order of magnitude at one specific level: that discontinuity IS field capacity, read directly off the probe's own index with no conversion. DAY (ET0 > 0) — moisture lost per mm of ET0 is flat across the plant-fed range (loss scales with atmospheric demand = transpiration-limited) and FALLS OFF at the dry end, where the plant starts restricting uptake; that falloff is the stress floor. Both numbers are properties of THIS soil, THIS probe and THIS calibration, and stay valid as long as the probe is not moved or recalibrated. RE-DERIVE (python3 lib/derive_bands.py) if a probe is reseated, moved to a new depth, switched to WH51L Custom calibration, or if the bed media is amended.

tomato._voltage_channel_comment: ADDED 2026-09-19 (#18). The WH51's console channel, used to find its battery-voltage column ('Soil Moisture Sensor CH1(V)', renamed by firmware to '[CH1] Tomato Soil Sensor(V)'). It was hard-coded in parse_ecowitt and substring-matched, so 'CH1' also matched CH10-CH16; adding the planned deep WH51L would have silently re-pointed the health check. Change this if the probe is moved to another console channel.

bands._comment: 3-inch WH51 in the 12x4 ft raised bed. Night-loss discontinuity is unambiguous: 0.17-0.76 %AD/hr below 75, then 1.66 at 75-79 and 12.07 at 80-84 — a ~16x step. Day curve is flat at ~4-5 %AD per mm ET0 across 50-74 and drops to 1.30 at 45-49, which is the uptake falloff.
bands.ceiling_confidence: high — n=1216 night intervals at or above it. Note this is drainage ONSET (75-79 runs 1.66 %AD/hr, ~4x the 0.44 baseline below), not the runaway point (80-84 runs 12.07). The ceiling is deliberately set at onset: a threshold placed at 80 would read as permission to fill to 80, which is the over-application this replaced.
bands.floor_confidence: LOW — the bed has spent almost no time below 50% (n=105 day intervals at 45-49, n=72 night), so the falloff is a hint, not an established threshold. Treat 55 as the practical watch line and do not deliberately dry the bed down to test this.
bands.leaching_fraction_note: Zero drainage is NOT the target. No summer rain here and municipal water carries real TDS, so 10-20% of applied water should pass the root zone to flush salts. A schedule that peaks just under drainage_ceiling delivers that automatically via the wetting front; one that never approaches it will accumulate salts.

bands._comment: 6x 7-gal fabric bags on the house controller. Night-loss step is at 48: 0.20-0.32 %AD/hr below, 8.85 at 48-50. Day curve plateaus ~1.5-2.1 %AD per mm ET0 across 36-44 and halves to 1.01 at 33-35 — the uptake falloff. NOTE the day curve for fabric bags conflates transpiration with sidewall evaporation, which is why the ceiling is read off the night data only.
bands.ceiling_confidence: medium — n=93 night intervals at or above it; the step is large (33x) but thinly sampled because the bags shed back past it within minutes. The DAY curve also runs hot at 45-47 (9.94 vs a 2.06 plateau), but that bin is dominated by post-run drainage rather than a real uptake change, which is why the ceiling is read off night data only.
bands.floor_confidence: usable — n=235 day intervals below it, with a clean ~50% falloff at 33-35 (1.01 vs a 2.06 plateau). Worth noting the retired hand-set pepper alert threshold was 35, within a point of the derived floor; that one was a good guess. The 30-32 bin reads a suspicious 0.00 on n=44 and is excluded by MIN_N_FLOOR — see derive_bands.py.
bands.leaching_fraction_note: Containers need MORE leaching than beds, not less — fabric bags accumulate salts fast and standard practice is a deliberate flush. Keep one long run every 2-3 weeks for salt management even though routine runs should stop at the ceiling.

bed._comment: Physical geometry of the metered tomato raised bed, recorded 2026-08-03. This is the missing conversion that makes metered litres interpretable as inches of water. Everything metered by the WFC01 lands on THIS bed only; peppers are a separate unmetered line.

target._comment: target_in_per_week is Justin's stated goal. NOTE it is a classic in-ground, moderate-weather rule of thumb; a 10-inch-deep raised bed in a Santa Clara August loses considerably more. august_etc_in_per_week is the estimated real crop demand (reference ET0 ~0.25-0.35 in/day x tomato mid-season Kc ~1.15). Water to the ETc figure in a heat event and drift back toward target_in_per_week in Sept/Oct. AMENDED 2026-09-19 (#22): august_etc_in_per_week is NO LONGER what panel 4 scores weeks against. It was one August figure drawn across the whole June-September span, and cached FAO-56 ET0 puts real weekly demand at 1.14-1.91 in/wk over 2026-06-29 -> 2026-09-19, below this constant in every week and below its lower edge from mid-August. Panel 4 now derives the band per week as that week's mean ET0 x kc_mid_season. The constant is kept because it is still a true August estimate and the dark CFG.bed template branches (#16) quote it.
target._kc_comment: FAO-56 crop coefficient for the tomato bed, recorded 2026-09-19 (#22). Panel 4's weekly demand band is that week's mean cached ET0 (mm/day) x 7 / 25.4 x this range. Mid-season only: there is deliberately no growth-stage curve, because FAO-56 tomato Kc_end ~0.7-0.9 was measured against this span and moved NO verdict -- applied depth was above every candidate band's top in all 11 complete weeks. Revisit when applied water gets close enough to demand for the late-season step-down to bind.

storage._comment: Plant-available water held by the whole 10-inch profile at an assumed AWC of 0.12-0.20 in per inch of soil. The point: a single 129 L dose is ~1.14 in, i.e. it tries to deliver most of the profile's ENTIRE available capacity in one 12-minute shot. That is why it drains.

emitters._comment: Audited 2026-08-03 against the measured 12.4 L/min line flow. Bubblers are adjustable 0-13 gph; back-solving from the meter puts them at ~13.4 gph each, i.e. WIDE OPEN, at or past spec. Do not throttle them far below ~half — the 8-stream full-circle pattern needs flow to distribute evenly, and a starved bubbler dribbles out one side. Use WFC01 cycle mode, not the bubbler threads, as the primary volume/rate control.

drip_flags.note: fixed rate; alone this is a 1.20 in/hr floor

infiltration._comment: The core problem found 2026-08-03. Instantaneous application rate is several times what the soil can absorb, so past the first minute or two water ponds, runs to the edges and channels down preferential paths instead of wetting the profile evenly. Effective (duty-cycled) rate should sit at or under the ceiling.

bed._plant_count_comment: UNKNOWN — needed to turn hand-application events into a volume calibration. On 2026-08-16 roughly 0.5 gal (1.9 L) per plant was hand-poured and the tomato probe went 71 -> 81 with +8 retained. With a plant count that becomes litres, and litres against the probe response is a DIRECT slow-application efficiency measurement to compare against the emitters' 19.9 L per 90 s pulse. Fill this in.

health._comment: Sensor-trust thresholds. nominal_volts is the voltage the probe's factory calibration assumes (1.5 V alkaline); a lithium AA reads ~1.7 V and shifts the derived moisture %. range_collapse_frac flags a probe whose daily AD swing drops below this fraction of its trailing norm (failing sensor or lost soil contact). volt_tolerance widened 0.08 -> 0.15 on 2026-08-09: a FRESH alkaline genuinely sits at 1.55-1.65 V, so 0.08 raised a false 'bad calibration' alarm on a healthy probe the day after the battery was restored. 0.15 still catches lithium (0.20 off nominal) while leaving normal alkaline headroom alone -- that gap is the whole discrimination this check exists to make.
health._range_comment: RANGE CHECK RECALIBRATED 2026-09-03 against the one labelled failure in the record: pepper Jul 22 - Aug 6, thirteen days at 4-6 AD counts while the tomato channel ran 97-145. That is a dead channel, and it is the only ground truth we have. Two changes. (1) ad_range_floor is now the `bad` trigger, because it is the only test that does not move when the irrigation schedule moves. 3-day-median AD range inside the failure was 4-9 counts; the minimum ANYWHERE else across 67 days and both channels is 15. A floor of 12 sits mid-gap, catches all 15 failure days, and produces zero false positives on the record. (2) range_collapse_frac dropped 0.35 -> 0.25 and DEMOTED to `warn`. At 0.35 the ratio test fired 11 times on a healthy tomato channel (Aug 10-15, Sep 1-3) and mislabelled the peppers on Sep 2-3 -- every one of those false alarms landed days after an irrigation regime change, because a flatter schedule IS a smaller diurnal swing and the trailing baseline still held the old regime's numbers. Real-failure ratios were 0.116-0.194 and nothing else went below 0.288, so 0.25 sits in that gap. Lengthening the baseline window does NOT help and was tested: 14d/28d/60d gave 7/11/10 tomato false alarms, because a longer window reaches further back into the high-swing pre-pulsed regimes. CAVEAT, and it is the important one: n=1. Both numbers are fit to a single incident, which is exactly how 0.35 got set. Re-derive when a second failure exists, and do not let the `warn` be deleted -- it is the only net for a failure mode that does not look like this one. AMENDED 2026-09-19 (#19): the zero-false-positives claim above was true to 2026-09-03 and is false now. Measured on 82 exports (06-29 -> 09-19), the range floor alone fires on the TOMATO channel on 09-12 -> 09-14 -- 3-day medians 10, 10, 11 -- so a page built on any of those days would have put the red badge on the channel believed healthy, and it fires on the peppers from 09-12 on a bag that is dry, not dead. The cause is structural rather than a bad constant: range conflates an excursion above a stable baseline with a day's net drift, and as the schedule shortened both channels' ranges fell toward the floor for the ordinary reason that a pulsed plan IS a smaller swing -- the same mechanism that demoted range_collapse_frac to `warn`, now reaching the absolute test too. ad_range_floor is UNCHANGED at 12 and is now one limb of a conjunction; see _excursion_comment. What stands from 09-03: the 12-count value, the n=1 caveat, and the instruction not to delete the `warn`.
health._excursion_comment: ADDED 2026-09-19 (#19) as the second limb of the `bad` grade, which now needs 3-day-median AD range under ad_range_floor AND 3-day-median excursion under ad_excursion_floor. ad_exc is a day's maximum less the HIGHER of its first and last sample: how far the trace rose above the line its own endpoints draw, which is drift-blind in both directions -- a day that decays 12 counts and a day that gains 12 both score 0, and only a genuine rise-and-return scores. That is what separates the two low-range regimes the floor alone cannot. Inside the Jul 22 - Aug 6 failure the excursion was 1-3 counts a day while the trace decayed 250 -> 203 with no diurnal cycle at all; across Sep 11-18 it was 4-8 counts a day, phase-locked to the morning run, on a drift of 0 against a floor pinned at 184-185. On 3-day medians the failure sits at 1-2 and everything else on the record at 4-8, so a floor of 3 sits mid-gap by the same construction as the 12. The conjunction selects exactly the 15 known-dead days out of 164 channel-days. NEITHER LIMB WORKS ALONE and both are load-bearing: excursion alone condemns any day that simply ends high (tomato Jul 12 and Jul 14 scored 0 counts of excursion on ranges of 42 and 48). Three caveats. n is still 1 -- this is fit to the same single incident as the 12, so it is no better calibrated, only measuring something the irrigation schedule cannot move. The nearest live point is one count away: Sep 19 medians 4 against a floor of 3, because a partial day ending mid-climb has almost no excursion, which is why both tests run on the 3-day median and not the latest day. And a probe that is dead but NOISY would pass -- stuck output with +/-4 counts of radio or thermal noise gives range 8 and excursion 4 -- so this tests for structure the Jul 22 failure lacked, not for a correct reading. The comparison is `< ad_excursion_floor`, so a tie falls toward not-dead deliberately: a badge that cries wolf is the worse failure here. AMENDED 2026-09-19 (#23): this floor now governs TWO tests, not one. onset_check()'s `no_data` gate was still scoring flatness on ad_range_floor alone -- the pre-#19 conflation, reached for by name -- so a missed run on the pepper line in the current pulsed regime would have published as an instrument gap rather than a valve failure, on the only run-log that line has; it now takes the same conjunction against the same two constants, on a trailing 3-day median. The WINDOW is load-bearing and is deliberately not the caller's: measured on 82 exports, this statistic taken over the trailing 24 h ending at the 06:45 slot reads 0-2 counts every day 2026-09-12 -> 09-18 on a channel cycling 6-8 phase-locked to that very run, because a window ending just after the run also STARTS just after the previous one and both endpoints sit on a peak. Per calendar day it separates the two low-range regimes as designed; on an arbitrary 24 h it says nothing, and a second limb built on it would have been a no-op that looked like a fix. Nothing on the published page moved -- no onset row changes kind -- but the counterfactual flips six slots (09-12, 09-13, 09-14, 09-15, 09-17, 09-18) that would have been graded wrong the moment a run was actually missed.

cycle_mode.REVISED_2026-08-03: Was 20/60. Lengthened to 45/135 (same 25% duty, same 1.65 in/hr effective rate) after Justin raised line-charge time. The hose must fill and the bubblers must reach pressure before real delivery starts; a 50-100 ft run holds 1.9-8.6 L depending on ID, which is 9-42 SECONDS of charge at 12.4 L/min. Against a 20 s pulse that is most of the pulse. Rule of thumb: ON >= 4-5x measured charge time. 45/135 cuts charge events per run by ~2.3x while keeping the effective application rate identical, because infiltration cares about the cycle-average rate, not pulse length. Per-pulse application at 45 s is 9.3 L = 0.082 in, which a 135 s soak clears comfortably at 1.65 in/hr.
cycle_mode.charge_accounting: RESOLVED 2026-08-03 with actual plumbing: 25 ft of 5/8 in garden hose = 1.51 L = 7.3 s of fill; the emitter manifold inside the bed adds ~0.96 L; total cold-start fill ~2.5 L / ~12 s. Crucially the hose runs UPHILL into the raised bed, so the emitters sit at the high point. When the valve closes, air enters at the bubblers and the hose water CANNOT flow back up over the crest — the 1.51 L in the hose simply stays there between pulses and between runs. It is never lost and never re-paid. Only the ~0.96 L above the crest drains, and it drains INTO the bed, so it is delivered rather than wasted. Net: NO volume is lost anywhere in this system. Within a run the effective re-charge is only the above-crest volume, ~5 s, so a 45 s pulse carries ~11% deadband on pulse one and near zero after.
cycle_mode.uniformity_finding: The real cost of cycling here is not volume, it is WHERE the drain-down lands. The ~0.96 L above the crest empties out of whichever bubbler sits lowest, once per cycle. At the originally proposed 20/60 that is 22 drain events/day and ~21 L/day preferentially dumped on one or two plants; at 45/135 it is 10 events and ~9.6 L/day; at 90/270 it would be 4 events and ~3.8 L/day. This is very likely a large part of why emitter output looks so uneven. 45/135 is the chosen middle: longer pulses cut the skew, but they also deepen transient ponding per pulse (0.082 in at 45 s vs 0.164 in at 90 s), which pushes water laterally to the bed edges. MITIGATION: find the lowest bubbler and either raise it level with the others or fit a small check valve just past the crest.
cycle_mode._comment: Manual: 'a duty cycle is introduced against the current working mode... can be used to regulate more precisely for lower water rate application.' Legal range 5-3600 s. 25% duty takes the 6.6 in/hr instantaneous rate down to ~1.65 in/hr effective, inside the raised-bed infiltration window. 20/60 gives ~4.1 L per pulse; 15/45 is a finer alternative at the same duty.
cycle_mode.RESOLVED_semantics: The app rejects On > Duration ('the on time cannot be greater than the duration'). That validation only makes sense if Duration is the total ELAPSED window that the pulses run inside — so Duration = elapsed, NOT ON time. The 4x ambiguity is settled and the duration_s column in the ramp table stands as written.
cycle_mode.APP_UNIT_TRAP: Entering Duration 360 s with On 45 s / Off 135 s was rejected even though 45 < 360. Near-certain cause: the Duration field has a unit selector (manual p25: '10~43200 seconds OR 1~720 minutes') that was sitting on MINUTES, so the form held 6 while On held 45, and the validator compared the raw numbers 45 > 6. FIX: switch the Duration unit to seconds and enter 360. If Plan mode only offers minutes, the only way to satisfy a naive numeric compare is On <= the minute number, which forces ~5 s pulses — volumetrically equivalent (On 5 / Off 15 for 6 min still gives 18.6 L) but useless here, because a 5 s pulse is roughly the above-crest refill time so nearly every pulse would be pure line charge.

The real risk is that the 2.35 in/wk ETc estimate is simply too low for a raised bed in a heatwave, while the probe is already at a record-low 50%. Abrupt swings also invite blossom-end rot and fruit cracking, so gradual is right regardless. THE PROBE SETS THE ENDPOINT, NOT THIS TABLE: hold at whatever step returns the overnight min to 58-60%, even if that is 70 L/day and the 38 L target turns out to be wrong.
